channel.title: AI - Ars Technica
channel.description: Serving the Technologist since 1998. News, reviews, and analysis.

item.title: Authors' lucky break in court may help class action over Meta torrenting
item.description: Judge gave authors an easier attack on Meta’s torrenting. Meta hopes SCOTUS ruling will block it.

item.title: With new plugins feature, OpenAI officially takes Codex beyond coding
item.description: Things are moving fast, and competitors have offered something similar for a while.

item.title: Senators want US energy information agency to monitor data center electricity usage
item.description: In a letter, senators press for mandated annual electricity disclosure for data centers.

item.title: Study: Sycophantic AI can undermine human judgment
item.description: Subjects who interacted with AI tools were more likely to think they were right, less likely to resolve conflicts.

item.title: The debut of Gemini 3.1 Flash Live could make it harder to know if you're talking to a robot
item.description: Google's new conversational audio AI is rolling out in search, Gemini, and developer tools today.

item.title: OpenAI “indefinitely” shelves plans for erotic ChatGPT

item.title: Reddit will require "fishy" accounts to verify they are run by a human
item.description: AI-generated content is still acceptable for now.

item.title: Google's TurboQuant AI-compression algorithm can reduce LLM memory usage by 6x

item.title: Disney cancels $1 billion OpenAI partnership amid Sora shutdown plans
